# SVG to Slides — editable SVGs in Google Slides

SVG to Slides is a free Chrome extension that inserts SVG files into Google Slides as native, editable shapes.

Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

- Install: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter (no install): https://svgslid.es/convert
- Google Slides add-on: https://svgslid.es/addon

## The problem
Google Slides doesn't support SVG files. Your options are to flatten them into PNGs or take the long way through EMF conversion, Google Drawings, and copy-paste.

## What it does
- **Edit individual elements.** Every SVG path becomes its own Slides shape. Recolour any element with the standard fill picker.
- **Resize without losing quality.** From a small footer icon to a full-slide graphic, every edge stays sharp.
- **Use SVGs in your themes.** Add converted graphics to theme layouts and reuse them across slides.

## How it works
1. Install the extension from the Chrome Web Store. No account required.
2. Open Google Slides, in any existing or new presentation.
3. Drag in your SVG. Its paths become editable shapes.

## Limits
- Gradients come through in the online converter; in the extension and add-on they currently collapse to a single solid colour.
- Arc commands (A/a) are converted into smooth curves.
- Up to 25 files per drop in the extension; use the online converter for larger batches.

## Questions
### Can you upload or import an SVG file into Google Slides?
Not as an editable graphic. Google Slides doesn't support SVG files. Install SVG to Slides and drag the file onto a slide, or convert it online at svgslid.es/convert. Every path arrives as a native Slides shape.

### How is this different from Microsoft PowerPoint?
PowerPoint can insert an SVG file and convert it to shapes. Google Slides can't. SVG to Slides gives Slides the same result: vector graphics you can select, recolour, and resize.

### Can I add SVG icons to Google Slides?
Yes. Drag up to 25 SVG icons onto a slide at once. Each one becomes editable shapes with no background box, so you can recolour it to match your theme.

### Do the shapes stay sharp when I resize them?
Yes. They're vector graphics, so a small footer icon and a full-slide graphic both keep crisp edges.

### Can I use SVG logos in my Google Slides theme?
Yes. Add converted logos and icons to your theme layouts and reuse them across slides. The shapes also work in Google Drawings.

### Is it free?
Yes. Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

## Privacy
The Chrome extension converts on your device with an embedded WebAssembly engine; your file usually never leaves the browser. Details: https://svgslid.es/privacy


---

# Convert SVG to Google Slides online

Upload SVG files at https://svgslid.es/convert and get a Slides-ready file in Google Drive with real, editable vector shapes.

1. Upload one or more .svg files. Each SVG becomes one slide.
2. Every `<path>` becomes its own native, individually selectable shape in Google Slides, not a flattened image.
3. The file is uploaded to Google Drive and a link is returned, optionally shared to a Google account you provide.

- Links are deleted after 7 days. To keep a file, open it in Drive and choose File → Make a copy.
- Solid fills, strokes and gradients come through. Arc commands are converted into smooth curves. Text is outlined into shapes.
- Clip paths, masks, patterns, filters and transparency don't come through. Tested results: https://svgslid.es/specs

Working in a deck already? The free Chrome extension drops SVGs straight onto a slide: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

# SVG vs PNG in Google Slides™

When Google Slides flattens an SVG it becomes a single image that blurs when resized and can't be recoloured or edited. SVG to Slides converts every path into Slides' own native shape format instead, so the result behaves like a shape you drew yourself.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## Flattened vs. converted

| Pasted as PNG (default) | Inserted with SVG to Slides |
|---|---|
| Blurs or pixelates when resized | Resizes at any size, always crisp |
| One flattened image, single object | Every path is its own selectable shape |
| Can't recolour without re-exporting | Recolour any shape directly in Slides |
| Can't animate individual elements | Animate each shape independently |
| Can't edit points or paths | Right-click → Edit points, like any native shape |

## Pick your route
- **Chrome extension** — Drag an SVG file straight onto an open Slides tab and drop it in place. No dialog, no upload step. (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi)
- **Web Uploader** — Upload one or more SVGs and get back a Google Drive link to a ready-made Slides file, one slide per SVG. (https://svgslid.es/convert)
- **Google Slides add-on** — Insert SVGs into a presentation you're already editing, from a dialog inside Slides itself. (https://svgslid.es/addon)

## How it stays a vector
- Every <path> in your SVG is converted directly into Google Slides' own native shape format. It isn't re-rendered as an image and it isn't a third-party embed.
- The result behaves exactly like a shape you drew in Slides yourself: resizable, recolourable, editable.

## Questions

### Does Google Slides support SVG natively?
Not as an editable format. Slides rasterizes an inserted SVG into a flattened image, so you lose the ability to edit individual paths or recolour parts of it. SVG to Slides converts it into Slides' native shape format instead, so it stays fully editable.

### What happens to gradients and complex curves?
Solid fills and strokes convert cleanly. Arc commands are converted into smooth curves. Gradients come through in the online converter; in the Chrome extension and add-on they currently collapse to a single solid colour. Tested results are on the specs page.

### Is my file uploaded anywhere?
Depends on the surface. The Chrome extension converts entirely on your device using an embedded WebAssembly engine, so your file usually never leaves the browser. The online converter and add-on send the file to our backend for conversion. See the privacy policy for specifics.

### Is it free?
Yes. Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

# How to insert an SVG into Google Slides™

Google Slides doesn't support SVG files, so you can't upload one as an editable graphic. To insert an SVG into Google Slides, install the free SVG to Slides Chrome extension, open your presentation, and drag the .svg file onto a slide. Each path becomes its own native Slides shape.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## How to do it
1. **Install the free Chrome extension.** Add SVG to Slides from the Chrome Web Store. No account required.
2. **Open your presentation in Google Slides.** Any existing or new deck.
3. **Drag the SVG file onto a slide.** Click to place it, then press ⌘/Ctrl + V. Its paths become editable shapes. Up to 25 SVG files per drop.

## Import an SVG without installing anything
- Web uploader. Upload one or more SVG files at svgslid.es/convert and get a Google Drive link to a Slides-ready file, one slide per SVG. Good for bulk conversion.
- Google Slides add-on. Insert SVGs from a dialog inside Slides, without leaving the tab. Get the add-on.

## Insert SVG icons into Google Slides
- Download icons as SVG files from any icon library and drag them onto your slide, up to 25 per drop.
- Each icon arrives as native shapes with no background box, so you can recolour it with the fill picker to match your theme.
- For a whole icon set, upload it at svgslid.es/convert and get one slide per icon, ready to copy from.

## The manual workaround: EMF and Google Drawings
1. Convert the SVG to an EMF or WMF file with a desktop or online converter.
2. Upload the EMF or WMF file to Google Drive.
3. Open it with Google Drawings.
4. Copy the shapes and paste them into your Google Slides presentation.
It works, but it's four steps for every file.

## The Microsoft PowerPoint route
1. In PowerPoint, choose Insert → Pictures and pick the SVG file.
2. Right-click the graphic and choose Convert to Shape.
3. Save the presentation as .pptx and upload it to Google Drive.
4. Open it with Google Slides and copy the shapes into your deck.
It needs a PowerPoint licence and a round trip through Drive for every graphic.

## Questions

### How do I import an SVG into Google Slides?
Install the free SVG to Slides Chrome extension and drag the SVG file onto a slide, or upload it at svgslid.es/convert. Both turn every path into a native, editable Slides shape.

### Can I upload an SVG to Google Slides directly?
Not as an editable graphic. Without a converter, your options are to flatten it into a PNG or take the long way through EMF conversion, Google Drawings, and copy-paste. SVG to Slides converts the file into native Slides shapes instead.

### Can I insert SVG icons into Google Slides?
Yes. Drag up to 25 SVG icons onto a slide at once. Each one becomes editable shapes you can recolour and resize without losing quality.

### How many SVGs can I insert at once?
Up to 25 per drop with the Chrome extension. For larger batches, use the bulk converter at svgslid.es/convert.

### Does it cost anything?
Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

### Is my file uploaded anywhere?
The Chrome extension converts on your device using an embedded WebAssembly engine, so your file usually never leaves the browser. The web converter and add-on send the file to our backend for conversion.

# Does Google Slides™ support SVG?

No. Google Slides doesn't keep SVG files as editable vectors. Your options are to flatten the SVG into a PNG, or convert it through EMF and Google Drawings. SVG to Slides converts the file into Slides' native shape format, so it stays editable.

_Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier._

- Install the Chrome extension: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/svg-to-slides/bdhhnakellmdnbgbdokiojipaebdeioi
- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## Flattened vs. converted

| Pasted as PNG (default) | Inserted with SVG to Slides |
|---|---|
| Blurs or pixelates when resized | Resizes at any size, always crisp |
| One flattened image, single object | Every path is its own selectable shape |
| Can't recolour without re-exporting | Recolour any shape directly in Slides |
| Can't animate individual elements | Animate each shape independently |
| Can't edit points or paths | Right-click → Edit points, like any native shape |

## Why Google Slides can't keep an SVG
- Slides builds everything from its own shapes, text boxes and images. It has no SVG import, so an SVG can only arrive as an image.
- An image is one object. You can't select its parts, recolour them, or edit their points.
- Resizing an image resizes its pixels, so edges blur.
- To stay editable, the SVG's paths have to become Slides' own shape format. That's the conversion SVG to Slides does.

## Which SVG features survive conversion
- Paths, basic shapes, arcs, transforms and even-odd cut-outs convert everywhere.
- Gradients and text convert on the web uploader, not in the extension or add-on.
- Clip paths, masks, patterns, filters and transparency are dropped. Full results for 20 tested SVG features.

## Questions

### Can you import an SVG into Google Slides?
Not as editable vector shapes. Install the SVG to Slides Chrome extension and drag the file onto a slide, or upload it at svgslid.es/convert. Both turn every path into a native Slides shape.

### Why does my SVG look blurry in Google Slides?
It's been flattened into a raster image, so it pixelates when you resize it. Converted with SVG to Slides, it stays a vector and every edge stays sharp.

### What happens to gradients and complex curves?
Solid fills and strokes convert cleanly. Arc commands are converted into smooth curves. Gradients come through in the online converter; in the Chrome extension and add-on they currently collapse to a single solid colour. Tested results are on the specs page.

### Do the converted shapes work in Google Drawings?
Yes. The native shapes also work in Google Drawings.


---

- Online converter: https://svgslid.es/convert

## Pick your route

## Which converter to use

| You want to | Use | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Drop an SVG into the deck you're editing | Chrome extension | Converts in your browser and pastes in place. No Google permissions. |
| Keep gradients, or turn text into shapes | Web uploader | Only the web uploader keeps gradients and outlines text. |
| Convert a whole icon set at once | Web uploader | One slide per SVG, in one Google Drive file. |
| Stay inside Slides without the Chrome extension | Google Slides add-on | Runs from a dialog in the Slides Extensions menu. |

## Every way to get an SVG into Google Slides

| Method | Result in Slides | What it takes |
|---|---|---|
| SVG to Slides Chrome extension | Editable shapes, one per path | Drag and drop onto the slide |
| SVG to Slides web uploader | Editable shapes, one slide per SVG | Upload in the browser, open the Google Drive link |
| SVG to Slides add-on | Editable shapes | Extensions menu inside Google Slides |
| Convert to PNG, then Insert → Image | One flattened image that blurs when resized | Any image converter |
| EMF or WMF via Google Drawings | Shapes, after several manual steps | A converter, Google Drive, Google Drawings |
| Microsoft PowerPoint, then import | Shapes, after a round trip through Drive | A PowerPoint licence |

## What each converter keeps
- Every surface converts paths, basic shapes, arcs, transforms and even-odd cut-outs into native shapes.
- Gradients and text come through on the web uploader only.
- Clip paths, masks, patterns, filters and transparency don't come through on any surface. See the tested results for 20 SVG features.

## Questions

### Do I need an account?
No account is required for the extension. The web converter takes an optional Google account email if you want the file shared directly to you.

### How long does the web converter keep my file?
The link stays active for 7 days. To keep a file, open it in Drive and choose File → Make a copy. The copy is fully yours, with no expiry.

### Is it really free?
Free forever. Every feature, no daily cap, no account, no Pro tier.

- **Animate each shape.** Build transitions element by element instead of animating one image.

## Questions

Yes, once it's converted. SVG to Slides turns each path into a native shape, so you can recolour any element with the standard fill picker.

Solid fills and strokes convert cleanly. Gradients come through in the online converter; in the Chrome extension and add-on they currently collapse to a single solid colour.

# Apps Script for GTM superpowers, part 1

*Nov 10, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Five scripts that turn Sheets into a launch control panel: a copy-length formula, one deck per account, follow-up drafts, a Monday digest and a change log. Slides, code and a cheat sheet.

## TL;DR
- Apps Script is JavaScript inside Google Workspace. Open a sheet, then Extensions › Apps Script.
- Five scripts: FITS() for copy length, buildDecks(), draftFollowUps(), a Monday trigger, an onEdit change stamp.
- Draft before you send, copy before you overwrite, read the permission screen.
- Slides embedded below, plus a two-page cheat sheet. Part 2 connects scripts to outside APIs.

Launch work in Google Workspace is mostly the same few moves, repeated: copy a deck, change the company name, paste a line from a sheet, draft the same email twenty times. Apps Script does those moves for you. It’s JavaScript that runs inside Workspace, it’s already in your account, and it needs no server.
Part 1 is five scripts a product marketer can run this week. The deck below walks through them. The post has the same code to copy, and the cheat sheet puts all of it on two pages.

Download the cheat sheet (PDF) (https://svgslid.es/static/blog/files/apps-script-for-gtm-part-1-cheat-sheet.pdf)

Make a copy (https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1MW2JGarOCNQnrnOQB96S4jwry3sLnud6JhM42LrvjK0/copy)
Present full screen (https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1MW2JGarOCNQnrnOQB96S4jwry3sLnud6JhM42LrvjK0/present)

## Where it lives

Open any Google Sheet and choose **Extensions › Apps Script**. That opens a script bound to the sheet: it can add menus to that sheet and react when someone edits it. Standalone scripts live at script.google.com and suit jobs that span many files. Everything here is bound to a sheet.

## First script: a GTM menu

    function onOpen() {
      SpreadsheetApp.getUi()
        .createMenu('GTM')
        .addItem('Build account decks', 'buildDecks')
        .addItem('Draft follow-ups', 'draftFollowUps')
        .addToUi();
    }

- Paste the code and click **Save**.
- Pick a function in the toolbar dropdown and click **Run**.
- The first run asks for permission. Read what it asks for, then allow.
- Reload the sheet. The **GTM** menu appears next to Help.

## Superpower 1: a formula that checks copy length

A function marked `@customfunction` works in a cell like any built-in formula. This one compares a line with its character budget, so overflow shows up in the sheet before it reaches a slide. It’s the check behind localizing a one-pager without breaking the layout (https://svgslid.es/blog/localize-one-pager-google-slides).

    /**
     * Says whether a line fits its character budget.
     * @customfunction
     */
    function FITS(text, budget) {
      const n = String(text).length;
      return n <= budget ? 'OK' : 'Over by ' + (n - budget);
    }

In a cell: `=FITS(D2, E2)`. Google’s custom functions guide (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/sheets/functions) covers what they can and can’t do.

## Superpower 2: one deck per account, from a template

Put tokens like `{{Company}}`, `{{Pain}}` and `{{Champion}}` on your template slides. Give the Accounts tab matching column headers. One run copies the template for every row and fills in the tokens.

    const TEMPLATE_ID = 'paste-your-template-deck-id';
    
    function buildDecks() {
      const [head, ...rows] = SpreadsheetApp.getActive()
        .getSheetByName('Accounts').getDataRange().getValues();
      rows.forEach(row => {
        const copy = DriveApp.getFileById(TEMPLATE_ID)
          .makeCopy('Pitch - ' + row[0]);
        const deck = SlidesApp.openById(copy.getId());
        head.forEach((key, i) =>
          deck.replaceAllText('{{' + key + '}}', String(row[i])));
      });
    }

Logos and icons on the template should be vectors so every copy stays sharp: here’s how to add a logo to Google Slides as an editable shape (https://svgslid.es/guides/svg-logos-icons-google-slides).

## Superpower 3: follow-ups as drafts, not sends

Rows marked Ready on a Follow-ups tab become Gmail drafts. Nothing is sent. A person reads every draft and clicks Send.

    // Columns: Name, Email, Company, Status
    function draftFollowUps() {
      const rows = SpreadsheetApp.getActive()
        .getSheetByName('Follow-ups').getDataRange().getValues();
      rows.slice(1).filter(r => r[3] === 'Ready').forEach(r => {
        const body = 'Hi ' + r[0] + ',\n\nThanks for the time today.';
        GmailApp.createDraft(r[1], 'Next steps for ' + r[2], body);
      });
    }

## Superpower 4: run it every Monday

A time-driven trigger runs a function on a schedule, with the sheet closed. Run `installWeekly` once. The digest checks the Days left column of a proof library (https://svgslid.es/blog/customer-proof-points-expiry-google-sheets) and emails you what expires within 30 days.

    function installWeekly() {
      ScriptApp.newTrigger('weeklyDigest').timeBased()
        .onWeekDay(ScriptApp.WeekDay.MONDAY).atHour(9).create();
    }
    
    // Proof tab: column G holds days left.
    function weeklyDigest() {
      const rows = SpreadsheetApp.getActive()
        .getSheetByName('Proof').getDataRange().getValues();
      const soon = rows.filter(r => r[6] >= 0 && r[6] < 30);
      if (!soon.length) return;
      MailApp.sendEmail(Session.getEffectiveUser().getEmail(),
        soon.length + ' proof points expire within 30 days',
        soon.map(r => r[1] + ': ' + r[0]).join('\n'));
    }

Google’s triggers guide (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/triggers) lists every kind of trigger.

## Superpower 5: stamp every messaging change

`onEdit` is a simple trigger: name a function that, and it runs on every edit, no setup. This one writes the time into column I whenever a row on the Messages tab changes.

    // Stamps column I when a row on Messages changes.
    function onEdit(e) {
      const sheet = e.range.getSheet();
      if (sheet.getName() !== 'Messages') return;
      if (e.range.getRow() === 1) return;
      sheet.getRange(e.range.getRow(), 9).setValue(new Date());
    }

## Test small

    function testFits() {
      console.log(FITS('SSO on every plan', 24));
      // OK
      console.log(FITS('Links that expire when you say so', 24));
      // Over by 9
    }

Run the test function from the editor. `console.log` output shows in the execution log, and **View › Executions** lists every run.

## Before you share a script

- Read the permission screen. It lists exactly what the script can touch.
- Scripts run as whoever runs them, with that person’s access.
- Draft before you send. Copy before you overwrite. Test on copies of real files.
- Quotas apply: one run stops at 6 minutes, and email has daily limits. See Google’s quotas page (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/services/quotas).

 (https://svgslid.es/static/blog/files/apps-script-for-gtm-part-1-cheat-sheet.pdf)
**The cheat sheet.** Two pages: where scripts live, how to run them, all five superpowers with code, the safety checklist. Print it or keep it next to the editor.
Download the PDF (https://svgslid.es/static/blog/files/apps-script-for-gtm-part-1-cheat-sheet.pdf)

## Coming in part 2: talk to everything else

Part 1 stays inside your Google account. Part 2 reaches out:

- **UrlFetchApp** to pull CRM and product data into Sheets.
- Launch updates posted to a Google Chat space.
- Gemini, called from a script, drafting copy to a character budget.
- A tiny internal web app with `doGet()`.

## What we have tested

- **Checked:** `FITS()` returns OK and Over by 9 for the two test lines above (run in JavaScript outside Apps Script). Every snippet passes a JavaScript syntax check.
- **Not yet run by us in Apps Script:** the menu, deck, draft, trigger and onEdit scripts. They’re written against Google’s Apps Script reference (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference). Run them on copies first.

More builds on the same sheet: update collateral from one messaging sheet (https://svgslid.es/blog/google-slides-collateral-messaging-sheet-gemini), Workspace Studio flows on shared files (https://svgslid.es/blog/workspace-studio-shared-files-messaging-flow), diffing Gemini’s deck edits (https://svgslid.es/blog/audit-gemini-whole-deck-edits-google-slides).

The screens in this post are mockups, not captures of Google’s products. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Forms, Google Meet, Google Chat, Google Drive, Gemini and Google Workspace and Apps Script are trademarks of Google LLC.

# Product screenshots go stale. Native UI mockups don't.

*Nov 10, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Every release breaks the screenshots in your decks. Build simplified product UI as native shapes and live text instead, kept in one library deck, and a renamed button is a find and replace.

## TL;DR
- Screenshots go stale every release, blur in print, and can’t be searched, recoloured or translated.
- A simplified UI mockup shows the one thing the slide is about, in your brand colours, at any size.
- Build components in Figma, export SVG, drop them into Slides with SVG to Slides. Shapes land native; labels go in as Slides text boxes.
- Keep every component in one library deck with a searchable label, so anyone can copy the current version.

## Why screenshots rot

A screenshot is a picture of one build of your product, on one screen, at one size. The next release renames a button and it’s wrong. Printed on a one-pager, it’s soft. Put in a German deck, the UI is still in English. And nobody can find which twelve decks use it.

[Figure: Left: a screenshot. Right: the same screen as native shapes and text.]

A simplified mockup fixes all four. It shows only what the slide is about, built from shapes and live text. It scales cleanly, takes your colours, translates like any text box, and a find and replace updates every label.

## Simplify first

A mockup is a diagram of the product, not a copy of it. For each slide, decide the one thing the viewer should see, and draw that.

- **Keep:** the layout, the element being talked about, the labels that explain it.
- **Drop:** real data, menus nobody looks at, avatars, timestamps, scroll bars.
- **Grey everything** except the element the slide is about. Colour that one.
- **Eight to twenty elements** per mockup. More, and it’s a screenshot again.

## Build in Figma, bring in as SVG

- **Draw components in Figma:** button, input, toggle, card, nav bar, table row. Flat fills and strokes. No shadows, blurs or gradients.
- **Keep text out of the SVG,** or delete it after export. Labels go in as Slides text boxes so they stay editable.
- **Export each component as SVG.** Figma’s export settings (https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/13402894554519) cover the options.
- **Drop it into Slides with SVG to Slides.** Drag the file onto your Slides tab, click where it goes, press Cmd/Ctrl+V. Every path becomes a native shape. Step by step: how to insert an SVG into Google Slides (https://svgslid.es/guides/insert-svg-into-google-slides).
- **Add the labels** as text boxes in your type styles, on top of the shapes. Group them.

Why flat: SVG to Slides converts paths, shapes, fills and strokes. Filters, clip paths, patterns and gradient transforms don’t convert. What Google Slides supports from SVG (https://svgslid.es/guides/does-google-slides-support-svg) has the details.

## One library deck

Put every component on its own slide in a single deck: the UI library. Under each one, add a small text label in white or light grey with its name, like `ui:button-primary`. Nobody sees it in use, but **Ctrl+F** finds it.

[Figure: The UI library. Each slide holds one component and a searchable label. Mockup.]

- When the product changes, update the component in the library. Note the date on the slide.
- To use one, copy it from the library. Don’t copy from an old deck.
- The same deck holds your icons. Convert an open-licence set once, one icon per slide, each with its label. That answers “where do I get icons for Google Slides (https://svgslid.es/guides/svg-logos-icons-google-slides)?” for the whole team.

## A renamed button is a find and replace

[Figure: One rename, every mockup in the deck. Mockup.]

Labels are live text, so **Edit › Find and replace** updates every mockup in a deck at once. Colours are fills, so a rebrand is a recolour: change the colour of any shape or icon in Google Slides (https://svgslid.es/guides/recolor-svg-in-google-slides) with the fill picker. And the same mockup works in Docs and Drawings, since it’s native shapes.
Logo designers build marks as vectors so one file works at every size. If you want to see that discipline up close, Will Paterson’s logo design channel (https://www.youtube.com/@WillPaterson) walks through it. Your product visuals deserve the same treatment: one source, every size, no blur. That’s the SVG vs PNG (https://svgslid.es/guides/svg-vs-png-google-slides) argument in practice.

## Where this fits

This is the visual side of the collateral system in part 1 (https://svgslid.es/blog/google-slides-collateral-messaging-sheet-gemini) and part 2 (https://svgslid.es/blog/messaging-workshop-brand-style-sheet-google-sheets): copy comes from the messaging sheet, visuals come from the library. Charts follow the same rule: draw them as native shapes (https://svgslid.es/blog/on-brand-charts-google-slides). And after any Gemini restyle, diff the deck (https://svgslid.es/blog/audit-gemini-whole-deck-edits-google-slides) to check the mockups weren’t touched.

## What we have tested

- **Checked:** a 16-element UI mockup SVG converted to 12 native shapes and 2 text boxes with the SVG to Slides converter and our placement script, and the shapes recolour with the fill picker.
- **Note:** the Chrome extension doesn’t convert SVG text. Add labels as text boxes, as above.

The screens in this post are mockups, not captures of Google’s products. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Forms, Google Meet, Google Chat, Google Drive, Gemini and Google Workspace are trademarks of Google LLC.

# Run a messaging workshop in Google Forms and build a brand style sheet in Google Sheets

*Nov 9, 2026 · svgslid.es blog · Part 2 of the collateral series (part 1: https://svgslid.es/blog/google-slides-collateral-messaging-sheet-gemini)*

## TL;DR
- A messaging workshop runs as a Google Form: 38 questions in 11 sections, built by script from a Workshop tab.
- Answers feed a five-level messaging architecture (primary; context, problem, promise; how; benefits and proof; secondary). Drafts come from =AI(); a person sets each of the 17 lines.
- The Messages tab takes each brief from the architecture and has Gemini write the line under a recipe per role and a character limit. No approval column. Adjunct tabs: Refinements, Audiences, Proof.
- Icons and UI mockups live in two master library decks of native shapes; asset decks pull from them by tag.
- Page recipes: twelve block formulas from seven live solution and product pages, filled in as two decks.
- A brand style sheet holds Colors, Type, Layout, Logo, Imagery, Voice, Personality and Gems, and exports itself as one text cell for scripts, agents and Gems.
- Worked example for SVG to Slides: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1EOSAfzAkwnhXBWwTkqBSMdMxF-BH9t50
- Starter pack: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12DEX6TnEHQ8goCO29j9ubwYfHP5K72-q

## Workshop sections
Company and focus; market; champion; target organizations; buying scenarios; awareness (1 to 5); needs (must, important, nice); selling proposition (unique, relevant, believable); sweet spot; message raw material; personality and tone (twelve archetypes, four tone scales).

Workshop tab columns: Latest response (newest form row, matched by question text), Override, Final. Everything downstream reads Final.

## Architecture
17 rows on five levels. Each row joins its workshop inputs into Source notes and drafts with the AI function (https://support.google.com/docs/answer/15877199):

    =AI("Promise. Write this element of a B2B messaging hierarchy from the workshop notes. One or two sentences. Plain, specific, active voice.", E6)

Example from our test: Gemini drafted "Convert SVG files into editable vector shapes directly inside Google Slides." The line we kept is "Editable SVGs in Google Slides."

## Style sheet
Type is set by role (eyebrow, headline, subhead, title, body, stat, label, cta, legal). The Messages tab gives each slot a role; the Apply style menu item sets font, size and colour on tagged text boxes. The Export tab joins all tabs into one cell of text.

## Gems
Message drafter, copy editor, image maker, image prep, asset checker. Paste the instructions into a Gem, then the export block. Availability depends on your Google plan.

## Libraries and page recipes
- Icon library (https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1aiPHjI3cdyQO8QnRu5GYpR2mLv0aFSCbSKramv4vOc0/edit): 85 Phosphor icons (MIT), one per slide, native shapes tagged lib:<name>, with a small white keyword label for Ctrl+F. UI library (https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1YiYVc8NgGR9VfWS5ySz5-0LwCbhVUtaRYRRBHdKrTpE/edit): 13 mockups.
- Asset slots are tagged icon:<key> and ui:<name>. Place icons and UIs swaps them for library shapes and keeps the deck's file ID. Add to library appends converted slides from svgslid.es/convert. The Icons tab has a searchable dropdown of library names.
- Page recipes (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ehY-jZ3Tq1q7070H8WEEniZr_yqYNPwik_4nHf-OCQE/edit): hero, proof bar, problem, pillar trio, feature row, benefit list, feature grid, how it works, FAQ, closing CTA, fact columns, testimonial. Solution pages keep feature names out of headlines until a grid; product pages name the feature first and explain the mechanism. Filled in as a solution page deck (https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/11x2sGv4ZbPbD1BBlyp9bVaXt2fYli2Ki6l2XpgXgY08/edit) and a product page deck (https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1cG0kRn9CByAw4vw6dv9H9lJBDx8SfAqwn8-bsuzlybA/edit).

## Test results (Nov 10, 2026)
- AI formulas written by script, import or API show as text until you click Generate and fill. One click covers a selected range. The 82 Line formulas had not been generated when this was written.
- Our first test account hit the monthly AI function limit after five cells.
- Gemini in Slides, on a Workspace account: a single-slide prompt applied three lines word for word and kept fonts, sizes and slot tags. The whole-deck prompt was refused; the rollout had not reached the account.
- Gemini in the Slides side panel wrote a 16-element SVG UI mockup to a palette-and-elements brief; it converted to native shapes plus two text boxes without edits.
- Dry run opened four decks and reported zero to three slots to change in each. Place icons and UIs worked after two fixes to mockup text (box width, type scaled from box height).
- Scripts ran on a sheet owned by the Workspace account that runs them. A personal account refused ("This app is blocked"); a sheet owned by another account showed an unverified-app warning. Link chips on the Assets tab break the script.
- Not yet run end to end: Sync all with generated lines, Add to library.

The screens in the post are mockups. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Forms, Google Drive and Gemini are trademarks of Google LLC.

# Update Google Slides collateral from one messaging sheet with Gemini

*Nov 9, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Write the brief once in a sheet. Gemini writes each line to a recipe and a character limit, and a script puts it in every asset. Updated Nov 10, 2026.

## TL;DR
- Since Oct 30, 2026, Gemini in Google Slides can edit a whole presentation from one prompt, grounded in a Drive file (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/10/edit-entire-presentations-with-gemini-in-Google-Slides.html).
- Point that prompt at a messaging sheet and one asset updates in one step.
- For exact wording across many assets, tag text boxes with `slot:<key>` in alt text and use a script or an agent.
- Gemini writes each line under a recipe, voice rules and a hard character limit. No approval column. Look at every changed page.
- Starter pack (templates, sheet, prompts, script): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/12DEX6TnEHQ8goCO29j9ubwYfHP5K72-q

## What changed
Slides could link charts and tables to Sheets, but not the text in a text box. Gemini's whole-deck editing takes one instruction, decides which slides it applies to, edits them in place as native text and shapes, and lists what it changed. Undo and version history work. Rollout began Oct 29, 2026 and may take longer than 15 days.

## Page sizes
- One-pager, solution brief, whitepaper: 8.5 x 11 in (US Letter) or 21 x 29.7 cm (A4).
- Battlecard: 11 x 8.5 in landscape. Sales deck: Widescreen 16:9.
- File › Page setup › Custom. Units: inches, centimetres, points, pixels. Set size before designing. One size per file.

## Bleed
Slides has no bleed setting. Add the bleed to every side of the canvas (Letter + 0.125 in = 8.75 x 11.25 in). Run colour blocks to the canvas edge, keep text 0.25 in inside the trim, draw trim and safe guides, delete them before export. Ask the printer for their bleed.

## Layout patterns
Six blocks: hero block, three up, proof strip, problem/answer, two columns with pull line, closing strip. Text boxes: fixed size with room to spare, one job per box, one style per role. Logos and icons as vectors (SVG to Slides).

## Messaging sheet
Columns: Key, Role, Source, Brief, Prompt, Line, Budget, Length, Fits, Used in. A person writes the Brief. The Prompt column joins the role's recipe, the voice and the row's budget from a Rules tab. The Line column is the Sheets AI function (https://support.google.com/docs/answer/15877199):

    =AI(E2, D2)

Rules tab: one recipe per role (eyebrow, headline, subhead, title, body, stat, label, cta, legal), the voice, "use only facts in the brief", "return the line only", and the budget as a hard character limit. There is no Draft or Approved line column (removed Nov 10, 2026). Needs a Google plan with Gemini. Nested AI functions are not supported. AI formulas written by script, import or API wait for a Generate and fill click. Only the Line column reaches an asset.

## Linked tables and charts
Copy in Sheets, paste in Slides, choose Link to spreadsheet. Tools › Linked objects › Update all. Updates are manual. Tables over 400 cells paste unlinked (https://support.google.com/docs/answer/7009814). Updates override edits made in Slides.

## Update one asset with Gemini
Prompt in the Slides side panel, with the sheet referenced:

    Update this presentation from the Line column of @Messaging sheet.
    Each row's Used in column says which asset it belongs to.
    Use the wording exactly. Do not rephrase, add or remove sentences.
    Keep every layout, font, colour and image as it is.
    Do not add or delete pages.

Limits: Gemini chooses which slides change; one file per prompt; availability depends on rollout and plan.

## Named slots and a script
Right-click a text box › Alt text › Title: `slot:headline`. The key matches the sheet. The script attached to the starter sheet adds a Collateral menu: Sync all (copy, style, icons and UIs), Sync copy to assets, Apply style, Place icons and UIs, Dry run. Over-budget lines and lines not yet generated are skipped and flagged. Untagged boxes are never touched. Deck URLs on the Assets tab must be plain text, not link chips. Instruction files for Gemini, Claude and Codex follow one agent contract.

## Rules, with approvals optional
There is no per-line approval step. Review the Rules tab and the briefs, read the Line column, run Dry run, sync, look at every changed page. Trade-off: nobody signs each sentence. For sign-off, File › Approvals on the sheet (https://support.google.com/drive/answer/9387535): lock for review; unlocking during an approval resets approvals; edits after approval leave it attached to the previous version. Approvals need an eligible work or school account.

## Layout shift
Slides does not shrink text to fit. Budget every slot, fix length in the sheet, skip over-budget lines, look at every changed page, update linked objects last.

## Tested / not tested (Nov 10, 2026)
Checked: templates keep page sizes and slot tags; budget formulas work; Dry run opened four decks and reported zero to three slots to change in each, no flags; Place icons and UIs swapped tagged icons and a mockup for library shapes and kept file IDs (mockup text sizing was fixed afterwards). Earlier: the AI function works after a Generate and fill click; a test account hit its monthly limit after five cells. On a Workspace account with Gemini, a single-slide prompt with three lines applied them word for word and kept fonts, sizes and slot tags; the whole-deck prompt was refused ("only able to edit the single currently active slide"). Not yet checked: the 82 new Line formulas (waiting for Generate and fill), and Sync all end to end. Part 2: https://svgslid.es/blog/messaging-workshop-brand-style-sheet-google-sheets

The screens in the post are mockups. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Drive and Gemini are trademarks of Google LLC.

# Google Slides finally does letter spacing

*Nov 7, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Tracking has landed in Google Slides. Here's what it is, how to use it well, and why Docs looks next.

## TL;DR
- Slides now has **letter spacing**, which type designers call **tracking**.
- Toolbar: the **|A|** button next to line spacing. Menu: **Format › Text › Letter spacing**.
- Presets: **6, 3, 0, −1.5**, plus **Custom spacing** (any value, decimals and negatives allowed; no unit shown).
- The Docs help center documents it; the Docs editor doesn't show it yet (as of Nov 7, 2026).

## Tracking vs. kerning vs. leading
- Tracking: same space added/removed after every letter in a selection (the new control).
- Kerning: space between one specific pair (e.g. AV); set by the font, not exposed in Slides.
- Leading: space between lines; the line spacing button.

## Tips
1. Open up all-caps text and small labels (+3 to +6).
2. Tighten large display headlines slightly (−1.5).
3. Leave body text at 0.
4. Bigger type → tighter; smaller type → looser.
5. Positive values widen lines: recheck line breaks and text box overflow.
6. One value per role (eyebrow, headline, body) for consistency.
7. Check in Present mode.

## Steps
1. Select text or a whole text box.
2. Click Letter spacing (|A|) in the toolbar, or Format › Text › Letter spacing.
3. Pick 6, 3, 0 or −1.5. Or choose Custom spacing, enter a value, Apply.
4. Reset by choosing 0.

## The slip-up that points to Docs
- Docs help article "Change how paragraphs & fonts look" (https://support.google.com/docs/answer/1663349) now has an "Adjust letter spacing" section (text, text boxes, tables; toolbar button and Format › Text › Letter spacing).
- Wayback Machine: absent on Oct 5, 2026 (https://web.archive.org/web/20261005194616/https://support.google.com/docs/answer/1663349?rd=1&visit_id=639268263719815361-3052973569); present Oct 12, 2026 (https://web.archive.org/web/20261012192940/https://support.google.com/docs/answer/1663349?hl=enGoogle:). Not in July–September captures.
- Docs editor Format › Text menu has no Letter spacing yet (checked Nov 7, 2026).
- Precedent: custom line spacing shipped to Docs and Slides together in Sept 2019 (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2019/09/line-spacing-docs-slides.html).
- No Workspace Updates announcement found yet. Strong signal, not a promise.

# Audit what Gemini's whole-deck edit changed

*Nov 3, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Gemini can now edit an entire presentation from one prompt. It tells you what it changed. Here is how to check, object by object, with a snapshot before and a diff after.

## TL;DR
- Since October 30, Gemini in Slides can edit multiple slides or a whole deck from one prompt, and it lists what it changed.
- For collateral with approved copy, check the list against the deck: text, fonts, sizes, positions, new and deleted objects, alt text tags.
- A short Apps Script snapshots every object to a sheet. Snapshot, run the prompt, snapshot again, diff.
- Anything in the diff you didn’t ask for gets undone.

## One prompt, many slides

On October 30, Google announced that Gemini in Google Slides can edit multiple slides or an entire presentation at once (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/10/edit-entire-presentations-with-gemini-in-Google-Slides.html). You can refresh fonts, backgrounds and colour schemes across a deck, restyle it to match another file, or condense and expand slides. Gemini decides which slides need to change and lists the changes in the side panel.
For a pitch draft, the list is enough. For a solution brief with approved wording, slot tags and a print layout, you want to know exactly which objects moved and which words changed. That takes a before and an after.

## The loop

[Figure: Snapshot, edit, snapshot, diff.]

- **Snapshot.** Record every object on every slide.
- **Edit.** Run your prompt in the Gemini side panel.
- **Snapshot again.**
- **Diff.** List every object whose text, font, size or position changed, and every object added or deleted.

## The script

Make a sheet with a tab called **Audit** and paste the deck URL into B1. Then **Extensions › Apps Script**, paste this, save and reload:

    // Bound to a sheet. Put the deck URL in Audit!B1. Menu: Audit > Snapshot / Diff last two.
    function onOpen() {
      SpreadsheetApp.getUi().createMenu('Audit')
        .addItem('Snapshot deck', 'snapshot').addItem('Diff last two snapshots', 'diff').addToUi();
    }
    
    function snapshot() {
      const ss = SpreadsheetApp.getActive();
      const deck = SlidesApp.openByUrl(ss.getSheetByName('Audit').getRange('B1').getValue());
      const rows = [['Slide', 'Object ID', 'Type', 'Tag', 'Left', 'Top', 'Width', 'Height', 'Font', 'Size', 'Text']];
      deck.getSlides().forEach((slide, i) => slide.getPageElements().forEach(el => {
        let font = '', size = '', text = '';
        if (el.getPageElementType() === SlidesApp.PageElementType.SHAPE) {
          const t = el.asShape().getText();
          text = t.asString().trim();
          if (text) { font = t.getTextStyle().getFontFamily() || 'mixed'; size = t.getTextStyle().getFontSize() || 'mixed'; }
        }
        rows.push([i + 1, el.getObjectId(), String(el.getPageElementType()), el.getTitle() || '',
                   Math.round(el.getLeft()), Math.round(el.getTop()), Math.round(el.getWidth()), Math.round(el.getHeight()), font, size, text]);
      }));
      const sh = ss.insertSheet('Snap ' + Utilities.formatDate(new Date(), ss.getSpreadsheetTimeZone(), 'MM-dd HHmmss'));
      sh.getRange(1, 1, rows.length, rows[0].length).setValues(rows);
    }
    
    function diff() {
      const ss = SpreadsheetApp.getActive();
      const snaps = ss.getSheets().filter(s => s.getName().startsWith('Snap ')).sort((x, y) => x.getName() < y.getName() ? -1 : 1).slice(-2);
      if (snaps.length < 2) throw new Error('Take two snapshots first.');
      const [a, b] = snaps.map(s => new Map(s.getDataRange().getValues().slice(1).map(r => [r[1], r])));
      const head = ['Slide', 'Object ID', 'Type', 'Tag', 'Left', 'Top', 'Width', 'Height', 'Font', 'Size', 'Text'];
      const out = [['Slide', 'Object ID', 'Tag', 'Change', 'Before', 'After']];
      a.forEach((r, id) => {
        const n = b.get(id);
        if (!n) { out.push([r[0], id, r[3], 'Deleted', r[10], '']); return; }
        for (let k = 4; k < head.length; k++) if (String(r[k]) !== String(n[k])) out.push([n[0], id, n[3], head[k], r[k], n[k]]);
      });
      b.forEach((n, id) => { if (!a.has(id)) out.push([n[0], id, n[3], 'New object', '', n[10]]); });
      const sh = ss.getSheetByName('Diff') || ss.insertSheet('Diff');
      sh.clearContents().getRange(1, 1, out.length, out[0].length).setValues(out);
    }

The **Audit** menu appears in the sheet. Each snapshot gets its own tab. **Diff last two snapshots** writes a Diff tab.

[Figure: A Diff tab after a restyle prompt. Mockup.]

## Reading the diff

- **Text:** compare each changed line with your approved copy. Paraphrase is the most common drift.
- **Font and size:** a restyle prompt should change these. A copy prompt shouldn’t.
- **Left, top, width, height:** moved boxes cause layout shift. Check the page.
- **New object / Deleted:** a deleted object loses its object ID and its alt text tag. If scripts find boxes by tag, re-tag the replacement.
- **Tag:** the alt text title. If you tag boxes like `slot:headline`, the diff shows which slot changed.

Two limits: the snapshot reads top-level objects, so shapes inside a group appear as one group; and it records the style of the text as a whole, shown as “mixed” when a box has more than one font or size.

## When something changed that shouldn’t have

Gemini’s edits work like your own: undo and version history both apply. Undo straight away, or restore the version from before the prompt and rerun with a tighter instruction. “Do not change any text” and “do not move or resize any object” are worth stating outright.
If your decks are localized, run the diff on every language version: a font change that fits English may break German. See localizing a one-pager without breaking the layout (https://svgslid.es/blog/localize-one-pager-google-slides). If a skill drives the prompt, the diff is how you test it: see Gemini skills for messaging recipes (https://svgslid.es/blog/gemini-skills-messaging-recipes).

## What we have tested

- **Not yet run by us against a Gemini edit:** whole-deck editing hadn’t reached our account when we wrote this. Google said rollout could take longer than 15 days.
- The script is written against the SlidesApp reference (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/slides). Run it on copies.

*Update, Nov 2026:* part 1 of our collateral series puts this to work: update Google Slides collateral from one messaging sheet with Gemini (https://svgslid.es/blog/google-slides-collateral-messaging-sheet-gemini).
The screens in this post are mockups, not captures of Google’s products. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Forms, Google Meet, Google Chat, Google Drive, Gemini and Google Workspace are trademarks of Google LLC.

# A competitor matrix where every cell cites its source

*Oct 29, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

AI-filled competitive research was unusable because nobody could check it. As of this week, Fill with Gemini attaches a web source to each cell. Build the matrix around that.

## TL;DR
- Since October 28, values generated with Fill with Gemini carry web citations per cell in Sheets on the web. Requests can cover up to 3,000 cells.
- Lay the matrix out long: one row per competitor and claim. It sorts, filters and cites cleanly.
- Add a Checked on date and a staleness flag. A citation tells you where to look, not that the claim is true.
- Only cited cells that a person has opened and confirmed reach the battlecard.

## What changed on October 28

Competitive matrices go stale fast and are tedious to fill. AI could fill them, but an uncited “Yes” in a pricing column is worse than a blank: someone repeats it on a call.
On October 28, Google announced that Fill with Gemini now provides cell-level citations for web sources (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/10/fill-with-gemini-now-provides-cell-level-citations-for-web-sources-and-supports-larger-requests.html). Each generated value gets its sources attached, and you can open them per cell in Sheets on the web. The same update lets one request cover far more cells: up to 3,000, according to coverage of the announcement.
That turns the AI-filled matrix from a liability into a first draft you can audit.

## Lay it out long, not wide

The classic matrix has competitors across the top and features down the side. It reads well and maintains badly. Use one row per competitor and claim instead.

[Figure: One row per competitor and claim. Mockup.]

- **Competitor** and **Capability:** “Acme”, “SSO on all plans”.
- **Value:** Yes, No, Partial, Unclear.
- **Evidence:** one short phrase from the source.
- **Source:** the URL you confirmed, pasted by hand during review.
- **Checked on** and **Status:** who confirmed it, and when.

Long format sorts by competitor, filters by capability, and pivots back into the wide view for a slide whenever you need it.

## Fill with Gemini

Select the empty Value cells and use Fill with Gemini, or write the AI function (https://support.google.com/docs/answer/15877199) directly:

    =AI("Using the vendor's public pricing or documentation pages, does "&A2&" offer "&B2&"? Answer Yes, No, Partial or Unclear, then a short phrase of evidence.")

Open the citations on a few cells before you trust the rest. You are checking two things: that the source is the vendor’s own page, not a reseller or a forum, and that it says what the cell says.

## Make staleness visible

    =IF(F2="","Not checked",IF(TODAY()-F2>90,"Recheck","OK"))

- **Not checked:** AI value, nobody opened the source. Never leaves the sheet.
- **Recheck:** confirmed more than 90 days ago. Pricing pages change.
- **Unclear** values are research tasks. Assign them.

## From matrix to battlecard

[Figure: Only confirmed rows reach the card, each with its footnote.]

Filter the matrix to Status = OK for one competitor. Those rows, and only those, go on the battlecard, each with a numbered footnote to its source. Reps can open the source in front of a prospect, which is the point. Put the competitor’s logo on the card as a vector so it prints cleanly: here is how to add a logo to Google Slides (https://svgslid.es/guides/svg-logos-icons-google-slides).
Customer proof on the same card has its own expiry dates. Track those in a proof library (https://svgslid.es/blog/customer-proof-points-expiry-google-sheets). Charts that compare you with the competitor should match your brand: draw them as native shapes (https://svgslid.es/blog/on-brand-charts-google-slides).

## What we have tested

- **Checked in Sheets:** the staleness formula.
- **Not yet checked by us:** cell-level citations. They were rolling out when we wrote this. We also don’t know yet whether a script can read the citations, so the Source column is filled by hand.

The screens in this post are mockups, not captures of Google’s products. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Forms, Google Meet, Google Chat, Google Drive, Gemini and Google Workspace are trademarks of Google LLC.

# On-brand charts in Slides, from Sheets data to native shapes

*Oct 26, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Sheets keeps adding chart types. None of them look like your brand once they're in a deck. Draw the chart as shapes instead, and every bar takes your colours and type.

## TL;DR
- Sheets added box and whisker, combo and multi-series scatter charts this year. Linked into Slides, they still carry Sheets’ look.
- Linked charts are right when numbers change weekly. For launch decks and printed collateral, draw the chart as native shapes.
- Bar charts need only rectangles and text boxes: a short Apps Script draws them on the current slide.
- Curves (lines, areas, donuts) come in as SVG with SVG to Slides. Labels stay as live text boxes.

## More chart types, same look

Sheets has had a busy year for charts: combo charts (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/07/import-and-create-combo-charts-in-Google-Sheets.html) and scatter charts with multiple x-series (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/07/create-and-import-scatter-charts-with-multiple-x-series-in-Google-Sheets.html) in July, and native box and whisker charts (https://androidauthority.com/google-sheets-adds-box-plot-support-3726846) rolling out in October. All useful for analysis.
Paste one into Slides and it still looks like Sheets: its own fonts, gridlines and colours. In a sales deck built on your type and palette, a default chart is the one thing on the slide that isn’t yours. (For why default type reads as default, Linus Boman’s video essays on typography (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCSb-xYOELhIqVr2n9s-b_4w) are a good watch.)

[Figure: Same data. Left: linked chart. Right: native shapes.]

## When to link, when to draw

| Use a linked chart when | Draw native shapes when |

| The numbers change weekly and someone clicks Update | The numbers are final for this launch or print run |

| It’s an internal review deck | It’s a customer-facing deck or one-pager |

| Accuracy matters more than look | It must match your type, colours and spacing |

Linked charts update from **Tools › Linked objects**. Google’s help page (https://support.google.com/docs/answer/7009814) covers how. Everything below is for the right-hand column.

## Bars: rectangles and text boxes, by script

A bar chart is rectangles and labels. Slides draws both natively, so a script can build one on the current slide from a range in Sheets. Every bar is then a shape you can recolour, and every label is text in your font.

    // Draws a bar chart on the current slide as native rectangles and text boxes.
    // Data: a two-column range (label, value) in the sheet named below.
    const SHEET_ID = 'paste-your-sheet-id', RANGE = 'Chart!A2:B6';
    const BAR = '#0066FF', INK = '#1C1E22', FONT = 'Verdana';
    
    function drawBars() {
      const rows = SpreadsheetApp.openById(SHEET_ID).getRange(RANGE).getValues().filter(r => r[0] !== '');
      const slide = SlidesApp.getActivePresentation().getSelection().getCurrentPage().asSlide();
      const max = Math.max(...rows.map(r => r[1]));
      const left = 60, top = 80, rowH = 44, labelW = 150, maxW = 420;     // points
      rows.forEach((r, i) => {
        const y = top + i * rowH, w = Math.max(2, (r[1] / max) * maxW);
        const bar = slide.insertShape(SlidesApp.ShapeType.RECTANGLE, left + labelW, y, w, rowH - 14);
        bar.getFill().setSolidFill(BAR); bar.getBorder().setTransparent();
        text(slide, String(r[0]), left, y, labelW - 10, rowH - 14, 'END');
        text(slide, String(r[1]), left + labelW + w + 8, y, 80, rowH - 14, 'START');
      });
    }
    
    function text(slide, s, x, y, w, h, align) {
      const box = slide.insertTextBox(s, x, y, w, h);
      box.getText().getTextStyle().setFontFamily(FONT).setFontSize(12).setForegroundColor(INK);
      box.getText().getParagraphStyle().setParagraphAlignment(SlidesApp.ParagraphAlignment[align]);
      box.setContentAlignment(SlidesApp.ContentAlignment.MIDDLE);
    }

Open your deck, go to **Extensions › Apps Script**, paste the code, set the sheet ID and range, select a slide and run `drawBars`. Change `BAR`, `INK` and `FONT` to your brand values. The SlidesApp reference (https://developers.google.com/apps-script/reference/slides) covers each call.

## Lines, areas, donuts: SVG to Slides

Curves need custom geometry, which a script can’t add to an existing deck. Draw them as SVG instead, in any tool that exports SVG, and bring them in with SVG to Slides.

[Figure: Data to SVG to native shapes.]

- Style the chart in brand colours before export. Flat fills, no gradients or shadows.
- Export as SVG.
- Drag the file onto your Slides tab with SVG to Slides and press Cmd/Ctrl+V. Every path lands as a native shape. See how to insert an SVG into Google Slides (https://svgslid.es/guides/insert-svg-into-google-slides).
- Add labels as Slides text boxes, in your type styles. SVG text is not converted, and live labels are easier to edit and translate anyway.

Native shapes stay sharp at any size, which matters when the same chart goes on a printed one-pager. The SVG vs PNG comparison (https://svgslid.es/guides/svg-vs-png-google-slides) shows the difference.

## Highlight one bar

[Figure: Click a bar, pick a colour. It’s a shape.]

The best reason to draw charts as shapes: you can make the point of the chart obvious. Grey every bar, then recolour the one that matters. Recolouring a shape in Google Slides (https://svgslid.es/guides/recolor-svg-in-google-slides) is one click in the fill picker.

## What we have tested

- SVG to Slides converts rects, circles and paths, which is all a flat chart SVG contains. Text and gradients are the parts to check after import.
- **Not yet run by us:** the `drawBars` script. It’s written against the SlidesApp reference. Run it on a copy.

If localized decks carry these charts, give the labels budgets too: see localizing a one-pager without breaking the layout (https://svgslid.es/blog/localize-one-pager-google-slides).
The screens in this post are mockups, not captures of Google’s products. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Forms, Google Meet, Google Chat, Google Drive, Gemini and Google Workspace are trademarks of Google LLC.

# Workspace Studio won't run on shared files. Design around it.

*Oct 13, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Studio flows fail on shared drives, shared folders and IMPORTRANGE. Messaging sheets are shared by definition. Here is the two-sheet pattern that works.

## TL;DR
- Google’s Studio guide: flows fail on Shared Drives, shared folders and sheets with IMPORTRANGE. Files must be private to you.
- Keep the team’s messaging sheet shared. Mirror it to a private sheet the flow owner owns, with a short script.
- The flow watches the private sheet, asks Gemini what changed and which assets it touches, and posts to Chat.
- October’s nested conditionals let one flow route headline changes and proof changes to different people.

## The wall

The obvious product marketing flow: when the messaging sheet changes, tell the team what changed and which assets need updating. Workspace Studio has a starter for “when a sheet changes” and steps to ask Gemini and notify a Chat space. It should take five minutes.
Then it fails. Google’s getting-started guide (https://support.google.com/workspace-studio/answer/16444479) lists the file restrictions: flows fail if you use Shared Drives, shared folders or spreadsheets with the IMPORTRANGE function, and files must be private to you. A messaging sheet that only one person can see isn’t a messaging sheet.

## Two sheets: shared for people, private for the flow

[Figure: People edit the shared sheet. The flow only ever touches the private copy.]

- **Shared sheet:** where the team writes and approves lines. Stays in your shared drive or folder.
- **Private sheet:** owned by the flow owner, shared with nobody, in My Drive. Holds a copy of the Messages tab.
- **Mirror script:** runs from the shared sheet and writes values into the private one. Values only, no IMPORTRANGE.

In the shared sheet, open **Extensions › Apps Script** and paste:

    // In the SHARED messaging sheet. Copies the Messages tab into a private sheet that the Studio flow watches.
    const PRIVATE_ID = 'paste-the-private-sheet-id';
    
    function mirrorMessages() {
      const src = SpreadsheetApp.getActive().getSheetByName('Messages').getDataRange().getValues();
      const dst = SpreadsheetApp.openById(PRIVATE_ID).getSheetByName('Messages');
      const old = dst.getDataRange().getValues();
      if (JSON.stringify(old) === JSON.stringify(src)) return;   // write only when something changed
      dst.clearContents();
      dst.getRange(1, 1, src.length, src[0].length).setValues(src);
    }
    
    // Run once to mirror every 15 minutes.
    function installMirror() {
      ScriptApp.newTrigger('mirrorMessages').timeBased().everyMinutes(15).create();
    }

Run `installMirror` once, as the flow owner. The script runs with that person’s access, so it can write to their private sheet.

## The flow

- **Starter:** when a sheet changes. Pick the private sheet and, if you like, only the Approved line column.
- **Step:** ask Gemini. “List the messaging rows that changed. For each, give the key, the old and new line, and the assets in its Used in column.”
- **Step:** notify the launch space in Chat with Gemini’s answer.

[Figure: What the launch space sees. Mockup.]

On October 9, Google added nested conditionals and new search steps (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/10/new-logic-and-search-steps-in-workspace-Studio-help-expand-automation-capabilities.html) to Studio. Use a condition to route by row type: headline and positioning changes to the PMM lead, proof changes to whoever owns the proof library (https://svgslid.es/blog/customer-proof-points-expiry-google-sheets).

## Limits to plan for

- **Delay:** a 15-minute mirror plus the flow’s own timing. Fine for messaging; wrong for anything urgent. The script only writes when the Messages tab actually changed, so the flow doesn’t fire every 15 minutes.
- **One owner:** the private sheet and the flow belong to one person. Document who, and what happens when they leave.
- **Usage limits:** Studio has per-user limits that depend on your plan.
- **Gems:** if an older flow uses an Ask a Gem step, it will stop working as Gems are phased out. See turning your messaging recipes into Gemini skills (https://svgslid.es/blog/gemini-skills-messaging-recipes).

For the meeting side of the same idea, see logging objections per slide from Meet notes (https://svgslid.es/blog/google-meet-notes-screenshots-slide-objections).

## What we have tested

- **Not yet run by us:** the mirror script and the flow together. The script is written against the Apps Script reference. Test on copies.

The screens in this post are mockups, not captures of Google’s products. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Forms, Google Meet, Google Chat, Google Drive, Gemini and Google Workspace are trademarks of Google LLC.

# Turn your messaging recipes into Gemini skills

*Oct 8, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Skills are replacing Gems as the way to give Gemini standing instructions. Write your copy rules once and call them with @ in Docs, Slides and Gmail.

## TL;DR
- Google is rolling out skills: reusable instructions for Gemini that work across the Gemini app and Workspace apps. Rollout in Workspace began October 5.
- A copy recipe is an ideal skill: fixed structure, length limits, banned words, a reference file.
- Call a skill with @ in the Gemini side panel. Gemini can also pick one when it fits the prompt.
- Gems are being phased out. Studio flows with an Ask a Gem step will stop working; rebuild them with skills.

## Skills, in one paragraph

On September 30, Google introduced skills in the Gemini app and Workspace (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/09/skills-gemini-app-workspace.html), with Workspace rollout from October 5. A skill is a named set of instructions, optionally with reference files, that Gemini applies when you call it. Google’s transition guide (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/generative-ai/gemini-app/about-the-transition-to-skills) says skills work in the Gemini app and in Workspace apps, while Gems can’t be used in Workspace apps, and that skills will replace Gems.
For product marketing, that is the missing piece. Your copy rules stop living in a doc people forget to open and start living where the writing happens.

## A recipe is already a skill

A messaging recipe says how a kind of line is built: what it starts with, how long it is, what it never says. That is exactly the shape of a skill.

[Figure: Anatomy of a copy skill.]

Here is one for headlines:

    Name: Headline recipe
    When to use: writing or rewriting a headline for a one-pager, solution brief, deck title slide or landing page.
    
    Instructions:
    1. Start from the approved fact the user gives you. Do not add claims.
    2. Lead with what the customer can do, in their words. Active voice.
    3. 6 to 9 words. Never over the character budget if one is given.
    4. No superlatives, no exclamation marks, no em dashes.
    5. Banned: "seamless", "revolutionary", "unlock", "empower", "next-generation".
    6. Return three options, each with its character count.
    
    Reference: @Brand style sheet (Voice and Type tabs)

Keep each skill to one job. A headline skill, a proof line skill and a battlecard rewrite skill beat one “brand voice” skill that tries to do all three.

[Figure: Three skills, one job each.]

## Using a skill

- Open the Gemini side panel in Docs, Slides, Gmail, Chat or Drive.
- Type **@** and the skill’s name, then the fact or draft you want worked on.
- Gemini applies the skill’s instructions and any reference files.
- Check the output against the fact. A skill sets the rules; it doesn’t check the claim.

Gemini can also recognise when a skill applies and use it without the @. That is convenient for writers and a reason to make each skill’s “when to use” line precise.
Admins switch skills on in the Admin console under Workspace Studio. If you don’t see them, ask your admin.

## What happens to Gems

[Figure: The transition, from Google’s timeline.]

- **Gems in the Gemini app** will be migrated to draft skills automatically, per Google’s transition guide.
- **Workspace Studio flows** with an **Ask a Gem** step will stop working. Rebuild those steps with skills or other actions.
- **Skills don’t sync** between the Gemini app and Workspace apps. To use one in both, create it in both.

## The recipe comes after the strategy

A skill makes rules repeatable. It doesn’t decide what you stand for. If the rules aren’t settled, settle them first: positioning, audience, the one thing you lead with. If you want an outside primer on brand strategy before you write recipes, The Futur (https://thefutur.com/) has a deep library on it.
Then write the recipes from your real best lines. Take three headlines you would ship today and describe what they have in common. That description is the skill.
Related: if your proof points feed these skills, keep their permissions current with a proof library in Sheets (https://svgslid.es/blog/customer-proof-points-expiry-google-sheets). If you train reps on the result, a Forms quiz (https://svgslid.es/blog/sales-enablement-quiz-google-forms) checks the message stuck.

## What we have tested

- **Not yet tried by us:** skills in Workspace. They had not reached our account when we wrote this.

*Update, Oct 2026:* Google later said the skills rollout in Workspace was running slightly behind its original schedule. Check the announcement (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/09/skills-gemini-app-workspace.html) for current dates.
The screens in this post are mockups, not captures of Google’s products. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Forms, Google Meet, Google Chat, Google Drive, Gemini and Google Workspace are trademarks of Google LLC.

# Customer proof points expire. Track them.

*Sep 9, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Logos, quotes and case studies come with permission, and permission has an end date. Keep a proof library in Sheets and get warned before a quote goes stale.

## TL;DR
- Every customer logo and quote you use was approved by someone, for some use, until some date. Write all three down.
- One row per proof point: claim, customer, scope, source of approval, expiry, days left, used in.
- A Workspace Studio flow can check the sheet weekly and post what is about to expire to Chat.
- September’s new Studio steps (Move Drive file, Copy Drive file) can also move retired assets out of the way.

## The logo strip nobody re-checked

A customer agreed to a logo on the website two years ago. Their champion left. The logo is still on the homepage, in four decks and on a printed one-pager. Nobody knows whether the permission covered print.
Proof points are borrowed. Treat them like anything else with a licence: record the terms, and track the end date.

## The proof library

[Figure: One row per proof point. Mockup.]

- **Claim:** the exact words you use. “Cut file transfer tickets by 60%.”
- **Customer** and **contact** who approved it.
- **Scope:** logo, name only, quote, case study, website, print, events. A dropdown keeps it consistent.
- **Source:** a link to the approval: an email, a signed form, a comment in a doc.
- **Expires:** the date the permission ends, or a review date if it has none. One year is a sensible default.
- **Days left:** `=IF(G2="","No date",G2-TODAY())`, with red under 30 and amber under 90.
- **Used in:** every asset that carries it.

The **Used in** column is what makes expiry cheap to handle. When a quote ends, you already know which files to open.

## Get warned before it expires

Workspace Studio builds flows from starters and steps, without code. A weekly flow with two steps is enough here:

[Figure: A weekly check, built from a starter and three steps. Mockup.]

- **Starter:** on a schedule, every Monday morning.
- **Step:** ask Gemini, with the Proof sheet as its source, to list rows with fewer than 30 days left, with the claim, customer and Used in.
- **Step:** notify the proof owner in Chat.

On September 2, Google added four new Studio steps (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/09/automate-drive-gmail-and-google-chat-actions-with-new-steps-in-Workspace-Studio.html): Move Drive file, Copy Drive file, Send a Chat reply and Reply to email. Move Drive file lets the same flow move an expired logo file from your shared assets folder to a Retired folder, so nobody drops it into a new deck.
One constraint to plan around: Google’s getting-started guide (https://support.google.com/workspace-studio/answer/16444479) says flows fail on files in shared drives or shared folders, and on spreadsheets that use IMPORTRANGE. Keep the sheet the flow reads private to the flow owner.

## On the page

[Figure: An expired logo, caught before the next print run.]

- **Logos as vectors.** A customer logo pasted as a PNG goes soft in print and can’t be recoloured for a one-colour strip. Add the logo to Google Slides as an SVG (https://svgslid.es/guides/svg-logos-icons-google-slides) and recolour it (https://svgslid.es/guides/recolor-svg-in-google-slides) to match the strip.
- **Tag each logo** in its alt text title with the proof row key, such as `proof:acme-logo`. Then a search, by hand or by script, finds every use.
- **Quotes keep their attribution** exactly as approved: name, title, company.

## What we have tested

- **Checked in Sheets:** the Days left formula.
- **Not yet built by us:** the Studio flow above. Starter and step names follow Google’s help pages; your Studio may label them slightly differently.

The screens in this post are mockups, not captures of Google’s products. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Forms, Google Meet, Google Chat, Google Drive, Gemini and Google Workspace are trademarks of Google LLC.

# Find which slide draws the objections

*Aug 12, 2026 · svgslid.es blog*

Meet notes now capture the slide on screen. Log each objection against that slide and the weak spots in your deck show up in a week.

## TL;DR
- Since August 3, Meet’s Take notes for me can embed screenshots of presented content, such as slides, in the notes doc.
- That ties what was said to the slide on screen. Log each objection with the slide it came up on.
- A simple Objections tab plus COUNTIFS shows which slides draw pushback.
- Presenters are notified and can turn capture off. Tell prospects notes are being taken.

## Call notes lose the slide

Call notes say “pricing concern” or “asked about SSO.” They rarely say which slide was up. So when product marketing asks which part of the deck isn’t working, the answer is a guess.
On August 3, Google started including screenshots of presented content in Meet’s meeting notes (https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/08/visual-screenshots-now-included-in-Google-Meet-meeting-notes.html). When you present during a call with **Take notes for me** on, Gemini can capture slides, charts and diagrams into the notes document, next to the summary. Now the notes know which slide was on screen.

[Figure: Meeting notes with a captured slide. Mockup.]

## Before the call

- **Present from Slides inside Meet.** Screenshots cover presented content.
- **Number your slides** and give each a short title in the speaker notes or on the slide. A screenshot is easier to log when the slide says “7 · Pricing.”
- **Tell the prospect notes are being taken.** Meet notifies the presenter that Gemini may capture screenshots, and the feature can be turned off from the notes panel. Admins can also require consent before notes start.

## After the call: one row per objection

Open the notes doc. For each objection, add a row to an Objections tab in your deck-feedback sheet.

[Figure: One row per objection, keyed to the slide. Mockup.]

- **Slide:** the number and title from the screenshot.
- **Objection:** one plain sentence. “Thinks SSO costs extra.”
- **Category:** a short fixed list: price, security, fit, proof, competitor, timing.
- **Quote:** the prospect’s words, if the notes have them.

Gemini in the Docs side panel can draft this for you from the notes. Ask for a table with those columns, then check each row against the notes before you paste it.

## Count by slide

On a Summary tab, list the slides and count:

    =COUNTIFS(Objections!C:C, A2)

Add a colour scale to the count column and you have a heat map of the deck. After ten calls the pattern is usually obvious: one or two slides draw most of the pushback.

[Figure: Objections per slide after ten calls. Illustrative numbers.]

Read the hot slides with the quotes next to them. Often the fix is a missing proof point or an unclear line, not a missing feature. Those are product marketing fixes.

## Automating the log

Workspace Studio has a starter that runs when a meeting transcript is ready, and steps that can ask Gemini and add rows to a sheet. That could write the Objections tab for you. Google’s starter guide (https://support.google.com/workspace-studio/answer/16765661) notes that this starter fires on the transcript, not on Gemini’s notes, so whether a flow sees the slide screenshots is something to test. We haven’t yet.

## What we have tested

- **Checked in Sheets:** the COUNTIFS summary formula.
- **Not yet checked by us:** screenshot capture itself. It was rolling out when we wrote this; availability depends on your Workspace edition and admin settings.

The screens in this post are mockups, not captures of Google’s products. Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Forms, Google Meet, Google Chat, Google Drive, Gemini and Google Workspace are trademarks of Google LLC.
